title: Operational GovOps can refuse to execute a rebate distribution and must publish its reasoning, with deadlock escalating to Core GovOps
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 builds a three-stage control around Grove's self-calculated rebate: "Operational GovOps reviews Grove's calculation of the rebate before executing a return of surplus to token holders. In the event of any issues, Operational GovOps cannot execute the distribution. If Operational GovOps does not execute the distribution, Operational GovOps must post an explanation on the Sky Forum under the 'Grove Prime' category and work with Grove to resolve the disagreement. If Operational GovOps and Grove cannot resolve the disagreement, it must be escalated to Core GovOps."

The wording is unusually strong: "cannot execute" is a **prohibition, not a discretion**. Where an issue exists, GovOps is barred from paying out — it has no authority to wave through a calculation it doubts, which removes the possibility of a quiet accommodation between the Agent and its own operator.

The design then closes the two obvious failure modes of a blocking veto. A veto could be used silently — so explanation is mandatory and public, in the same forum category used for governance proposals. And a veto could produce indefinite stalemate — so unresolved disagreement "must be escalated to Core GovOps," a Sky-level function outside the Grove relationship.

This is the Atlas's general shape for operational disputes: **self-calculation, independent blocking review, forced publicity, named escalation**. The party with the information does the arithmetic; the party with no stake in the answer holds the release; the ecosystem gets the record either way.
description: Because Grove self-calculates the rebate it deducts, the check is a blocking review with a forced public explanation and a named escalation path — not an advisory sign-off.
